tasks.short: Counsel individuals, groups or families in sessions, write session notes, record goals and the action plan, and schedule follow-up sessions.

steps.what: Psychologist counsels individuals, groups or families to help them deal with crisis situations and define goals

loop.input: The psychologist's spoken summary after the session and the client's goals in the record.
loop.output: A draft session note in the record's format.
loop.check: A validator flags any goal, risk statement or medication that does not match the record; the psychologist corrects and approves before the note is saved.
loop.stop: One draft per session; if the psychologist rejects it, they write the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sessions vary; a fixed form does not capture what was discussed.

steps.what: Psychologist records goals and the realistic action plan in the record
Psychologist schedules follow-up sessions by phone

tasks.design: After a session, the psychologist speaks a short summary and speech-driven reporting drafts the note; a validator flags goals, risk statements and medication that do not match the record, and the psychologist approves before saving. Goals and the action plan go into a structured template in the record ({OTHER}). Clients book follow-ups in the client portal from the psychologist's open slots. Counselling stays with the psychologist; sessions are not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after each session and follow-ups booked by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-driven reporting is used by most large mental health providers.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add statements the psychologist did not make.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm with a family in crisis.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist corrects drafts instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether notes are complete on the day.

evidence.claim: 24 of 25 large Dutch mental health providers use speech-driven reporting.
At a London NHS child mental health clinic, median admin time per encounter fell from 27 to 10 minutes with ambient voice notes (10 clinicians).
The psychologist stays accountable for AI-drafted notes.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session booked to the follow-up booked; referral to other care is outside.
Input contract: goals in the record; fallback is typing notes.
Clients book online in about the time a call took; a little client time is priced.
A DPIA and works council consent come before use.
research_questions: How long does correcting drafts take?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short notes; high: many sessions with long notes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with clients to help them gain insight and plan action, give exercises and homework, and note the session.

steps.what: Psychologist interacts with clients to assist them in gaining insight and defining goals
Psychologist prepares exercises and homework materials for the client
Psychologist notes the session in the record

loop.input: The psychologist's spoken summary after the session and the client's goals.
loop.check: A validator flags any goal or risk statement that does not match the record; the psychologist corrects and approves.
loop.stop: One draft per session; if rejected, the psychologist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Insight work is told in free speech; a form does not capture it.

tasks.design: Exercises and homework come from a library of standard modules in the client portal that the psychologist assigns and adapts, instead of preparing handouts each time. Session notes are drafted from the psychologist's spoken summary and checked by a validator against the record; the psychologist approves before saving. Talking with clients stays with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts were prepared per client and notes typed after sessions.
tasks.enabler_now: Client portals hold exercise modules; speech-driven reporting drafts notes.
tasks.still_hard: Standard exercises do not fit every client.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that opens up a client's insight.

reach.learn: Whether homework is done more often.

evidence.claim: 24 of 25 large Dutch mental health providers use speech-driven reporting.
Session notes are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session booked to the session noted; treatment evaluation is outside.
Input contract: module library kept by the practice; fallback is handouts.
Clients do homework in the portal in about the time handouts took.

incremental.description: Psychologist keeps the module library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few exercises; high: many sessions with homework.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the referral and case history, interview the client, administer tests and questionnaires, score them against norm tables, and write the intake report.

steps.what: Psychologist reads the referral and case history
Psychologist collects information about clients using interviews and observational techniques
Psychologist administers tests and questionnaires on paper
Psychologist scores the assessment methods against norm tables by hand

tasks.design: Referrals and earlier care data arrive in the record ({OTHER}) through the secure care exchange. Clients complete standard questionnaires online before the intake, and code scores them against the norm tables, so the psychologist does not hand them out or score by hand. The intake report template pulls in the scores. Interviewing, observing and judging stay with the psychologist; tests that need supervision are still taken in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questionnaires were done on paper and scored by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Online questionnaires with norm-table scoring are standard in mental health care.
tasks.still_hard: Some tests are licensed only for supervised use.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a client avoids saying in the intake.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist interprets scores instead of computing them.

evidence.claim: Test scoring against norm tables is plain code.
Test results are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the intake report; diagnosis is outside.
Input contract: test licences allow online use; fallback is paper.
Clients fill questionnaires online in about the time paper took.

incremental.description: Psychologist checks that questionnaires were completed before intake.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: supervised tests; high: standard online questionnaires.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect outcome questionnaires, review scores and progress, evaluate the effectiveness of treatment and the diagnosis, discuss with the client, and update the plan and diagnosis.

steps.what: Psychologist hands out and collects outcome questionnaires on paper
Psychologist reviews outcome scores and progress
Psychologist evaluates the effectiveness of treatments and the accuracy of diagnoses
Psychologist discusses the evaluation with the client
Psychologist modifies plans or diagnoses in the record

tasks.design: Outcome questionnaires go to clients online at set moments in the treatment, and code scores them, so the psychologist does not hand out and collect paper. A progress view in the record ({OTHER}) shows scores over time against the expected course. The treatment plan template carries the current goals and diagnosis forward for editing. Evaluating effectiveness and diagnoses and discussing them with the client stay with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outcome questionnaires were handled on paper and progress read from loose scores.
tasks.enabler_now: Online outcome measurement with automatic scoring is common in mental health care.
tasks.still_hard: Scores do not show why a treatment is not working.
tasks.human_edge: Admitting to a client that the diagnosis needs revising.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist reads trends instead of collecting scores.

reach.learn: Whether clients who do not improve are seen sooner.

evidence.claim: Online outcome questionnaires with automatic scoring and progress views are common in mental health care.
Research on special-category data without consent must meet four joint conditions.

assumptions: Boundary: from the evaluation due to the plan updated; referral is outside.
Input contract: clients have portal access; fallback is paper.
Clients fill questionnaires online in about the time paper took.
Outcome scores are not used to rate psychologists without works council consent.

incremental.description: Psychologist follows up clients who do not complete questionnaires.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few evaluations; high: many clients with regular outcome measurement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The psychologist keeps counselling, interviewing and evaluating treatment; typed notes, hand scoring and paper questionnaires shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A psychologist with more time for clients.
